key_insight: DiT-Reward shows that a text-to-image generator can be repurposed as a reward model, using generative representations to judge image quality and text alignment. The key idea is that near-clean image latents and layer-wise transformer features contain enough information to predict rewards effectively.
problem_solved: Text-to-image systems need reliable reward models to evaluate generated images, but standard reward models may not fully leverage the rich representations learned during image generation. This paper addresses how to turn a pretrained diffusion transformer into an effective evaluator for generated images.
method: Start with a pretrained text-to-image Diffusion Transformer (DiT) instead of training a separate reward model from scratch.
Process near-clean image latents so the model focuses on evaluating generated content rather than noisy intermediate states.
Aggregate text-conditioned image representations across multiple transformer layers to produce reward predictions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more efficient way to build image reward models by reusing generative backbones. It may improve alignment evaluation for text-to-image systems while reducing the need for separate model architectures.
